outcomes: Represent binary segmentation logits and masks consistently and compute Dice and IoU with explicit empty-mask behavior.
Use automatic and point-prompt foundation-model segmentation while measuring sensitivity to preprocessing and prompts.
Generate an auditable pseudo-label dataset that preserves source identity, model revision, prompt, and review status.
Fine-tune and evaluate a semantic segmenter with paired image/mask transforms, safe checkpoints, and patient-level splits.
Distinguish useful transfer from clinical validity and document licensing, provenance, and failure modes.

sections.title: Define the pixel-level contract before choosing a model
sections.summary: Segmentation maps each spatial location to a class, so logits, masks, thresholds, and reductions must agree.
body: For binary segmentation, a model can return one logit channel [B, 1, H, W] and use BCEWithLogitsLoss, or two class logits and cross-entropy. Ground-truth masks are spatial targets, not RGB pictures. Preserve them as boolean or integer class tensors and never normalize their label values like image intensities.

Dice and IoU summarize overlap after a threshold or argmax. Keep training loss and reporting metric as separate functions, define whether reduction happens per image or over the batch, and explicitly handle the case where both prediction and target are empty.
points: Logits are unbounded model outputs; probabilities come from sigmoid or softmax.
Masks must share the image's transformed geometry.
A threshold belongs to the validation-selected decision rule.
Report overlap with failure counts and representative examples.

callouts.title: Smooth terms define behavior
callouts.body: An epsilon makes division finite and makes this implementation return 1 when both sums are exactly zero. State whether that is the reporting policy and test empty target, empty prediction, and both empty.

sections.title: Compare automatic masks with explicit prompts
sections.summary: Foundation models can propose many masks or condition a prediction on points, but neither mode knows the medical task automatically.
body: Automatic mask generation can reveal how a general model partitions an ordinary image. Inspect mask area, confidence fields, overlaps, and nested regions rather than displaying every colored proposal as equally meaningful. A point prompt supplies a stronger hypothesis, yet small coordinate changes can select a different object or subregion.

Use positive and negative prompt examples, preserve original image dimensions, and plot the prompt on the exact image given to the processor. Coordinate transforms introduced by resize or padding must be owned by the processor or reproduced exactly.
points: Automatic proposals require a task-specific selection rule.
A point location is part of the model input and must be logged.
Confidence is not a substitute for ground-truth overlap.
Prompt sensitivity should be measured, not illustrated once.

sections.title: Bridge CT slices to an image-trained model transparently
sections.summary: Replicating a grayscale slice into RGB satisfies a shape requirement but does not erase the domain shift.
body: Select and document a CT window, clip intensities, scale them to the processor's expected range, and create three channels only when the external model requires them. Plot the original intensity slice, windowed input, candidate point, and resulting mask together so preprocessing failures remain visible.

A candidate center expressed in volume coordinates must be converted to slice pixel coordinates without swapping axes. Test a known landmark and preserve series UID, slice index, world center, window, processor revision, and prompt in the output record.

callouts.title: Shape compatibility is not domain validity
callouts.body: An RGB-shaped CT tensor can run through an image model while producing medically meaningless masks. Ground-truth review and domain evaluation remain necessary.

sections.title: Treat generated masks as pseudo-labels, not ground truth
sections.summary: A useful generated dataset records how every mask was produced and whether it was reviewed.
body: For each source slice, save a lossless image or tensor, a discrete mask, and structured metadata. Include source series, slice, candidate center, preprocessing window, model and processor revision, prompt, selection rule, generated score, timestamp, and review status. Store train, validation, and test membership from the original identity split.

Do not split generated images randomly after export. Multiple slices, prompts, or masks derived from one CT series remain related. Review a stratified sample before fine-tuning and version any filtering rule so later results can be traced to a specific pseudo-label release.

code.title: A provenance-rich pseudo-label record
code.source:
def make_pseudo_label_record(
    *,
    series_uid,
    slice_index,
    candidate_world_xyz,
    prompt_xy,
    window_hu,
    model_revision,
    processor_revision,
    selection_rule,
    generated_score,
    created_at_utc,
    image_path,
    mask_path,
    split,
    review_status="unreviewed",
):
    candidate_world_xyz = [float(value) for value in candidate_world_xyz]
    prompt_xy = [float(value) for value in prompt_xy]
    window_hu = [float(value) for value in window_hu]
    if len(candidate_world_xyz) != 3 or len(prompt_xy) != 2 or len(window_hu) != 2:
        raise ValueError("expected XYZ, XY, and [low, high] coordinate contracts")

    return {
        "series_uid": str(series_uid),
        "slice_index": int(slice_index),
        "candidate_world_xyz": candidate_world_xyz,
        "prompt_xy": prompt_xy,
        "window_hu": window_hu,
        "model_revision": str(model_revision),
        "processor_revision": str(processor_revision),
        "selection_rule": str(selection_rule),
        "generated_score": float(generated_score),
        "created_at_utc": str(created_at_utc),
        "image_path": str(image_path),
        "mask_path": str(mask_path),
        "review_status": str(review_status),
        "split": str(split),
    }

sections.title: Transform images and masks with one random decision
sections.summary: TorchVision transforms v2 can apply supported geometry consistently to an Image and Mask tensor.
body: Wrap the image and mask with their semantic tv_tensor types, then pass them through one v2 transform pipeline. Geometric transforms dispatch appropriately: image interpolation can be bilinear while discrete masks preserve class IDs. Photometric transforms should affect the image only.

Current TorchVision recommends transforms v2 because it supports images, masks, boxes, videos, keypoints, and arbitrary nested structures. Still inspect transformed pairs and add a synthetic landmark test; API-level pairing cannot prove a transformation is anatomically appropriate.

sections.title: Fine-tune a segmenter with a reproducible boundary
sections.summary: A pretrained processor, model head, loss, optimizer, and split together define the experiment.
body: Confirm the processor's rescaling and normalization so the dataset does not apply them twice. Verify label IDs, ignore index, output resolution, and how logits are resized back to the mask shape. Start by overfitting a few reviewed masks before a full pseudo-label run.

Use AdamW, current AMP APIs where beneficial, and validation overlap for checkpoint selection. Save trusted state_dict checkpoints with model/processor revisions and split release. Reload into reconstructed code with weights_only=True and compare fixed-image logits before continuing.

code.title: Checkpoint the fine-tuning state
code.source:
import torch

def save_training_checkpoint(
    checkpoint_path,
    model,
    optimizer,
    epoch,
    model_revision,
    processor_revision,
    dataset_revision,
    split_revision,
    validation_dice,
):
    torch.save({
        "model": model.state_dict(),
        "optimizer": optimizer.state_dict(),
        "epoch": int(epoch),
        "model_revision": str(model_revision),
        "processor_revision": str(processor_revision),
        "dataset_revision": str(dataset_revision),
        "split_revision": str(split_revision),
        "validation_dice": float(validation_dice),
    }, checkpoint_path)

sections.title: Evaluate transfer, speed, and limitations together
sections.summary: SAM-style masks, DINO-style embeddings, and a fine-tuned segmenter answer different questions and require separate evidence.
body: Embedding models can support retrieval or feature analysis without directly producing a task mask. Promptable segmentation can reduce annotation effort but introduces prompt and selection policy. A fine-tuned semantic model can make repeatable predictions but inherits pseudo-label errors. Compare these roles rather than ranking unlike outputs as one leaderboard.

For inference, use model.eval() and torch.inference_mode. After eager parity, SDPA and torch.compile may accelerate attention-heavy encoders. Measure first-call cost, warm latency, memory, and overlap because reduced precision or compilation can alter mask boundaries. Record external model licenses and model-card limitations with every published result.

code.title: Verify compiled mask logits
code.source:
import torch

def compile_after_parity_check(model, pixel_values):
    model.eval()
    compiled_model = torch.compile(model)
    with torch.inference_mode():
        eager = model(pixel_values).logits
        _ = compiled_model(pixel_values).logits  # compile and warm
        compiled = compiled_model(pixel_values).logits
    torch.testing.assert_close(compiled, eager, rtol=2e-3, atol=2e-3)
    return compiled_model
